## The question

> What happens to a photo after you post it?

**The walkaway:**

> Copies, caches, screenshots and metadata. Deleting removes one of those four.

## Script

| # | In | Type | s | Narration | Caption text (board) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 0:00.0 | hook | 4.0 | You posted one photo. Seconds later there were copies you will never see. | Copies you will never see |
| 2 | 0:04.0 | title | 3.0 | What actually happens when you post. | After you press post |
| 3 | 0:07.0 | explain | 7.0 | Your phone sends it up. The app immediately makes several smaller versions. | Several smaller versions |
| 4 | 0:14.0 | explain | 8.0 | Those copies sit on servers in many cities, near the people who will view them. | Copies in many cities |
| 5 | 0:22.0 | explain | 7.0 | And every viewer's phone keeps its own copy, quietly, to load it faster. | A copy on their phone |
| 6 | 0:29.0 | explain | 7.0 | A screenshot is also a copy. The app cannot delete it, ever. | A screenshot is a copy |
| 7 | 0:36.0 | myth-check | 8.0 | Deleting removes your copy and the public link. Not the screenshots. | Delete is not a recall |
| 8 | 0:44.0 | explain | 8.0 | The photo can also carry hidden data: where it was taken, when, and on what. | Hidden data inside |
| 9 | 0:52.0 | step-by-step | 9.0 | Three habits. Strip the location. Share to a small group first. Assume it is permanent. | Three habits |
| 10 | 1:01.0 | explain | 7.0 | None of this is a reason to stop posting. It is a reason to post on purpose. | Post on purpose |
| 11 | 1:08.0 | recap | 5.0 | Copies. Caches. Screenshots. Metadata. | What a post becomes |
| 12 | 1:13.0 | outro | 3.0 | Post like it is permanent. Because the internet already does. | Episode 05 |
